title: The Concept of A Priori Knowledge
text:
A priori knowledge refers to understanding or truth that is independent of experience. These types of truths are considered necessary and universal, often relating to logic or mathematics.

The Enlightenment philosopher Immanuel Kant distinguished this form of knowledge from a posteriori knowledge, which derives directly from sensory observation or empirical evidence. While empirical investigation builds our practical understanding of the world, pure reason grants access to structural concepts that hold true regardless of what might be observed in reality.
This distinction fundamentally shapes epistemology by establishing categories for determining the limits and scope of human understanding.
